releases.notes:
### Player
- Windows: ASIO audio interfaces in the preview player. Right-click the speaker, *Output device…*, and pick ASIO
  as the device type (beside Windows Audio and DirectSound). Most ASIO drivers serve one app at a time, so close
  Engine DJ or Serato first if they hold the same interface.
- Cue output (#67): on an interface with more than two outputs, *Output device…* lets you tick the pair the preview
  plays on (3/4 for headphones or cue). Remembered for each device; back to 1/2 if a device no longer has that pair.
  The speaker's menu says where it's playing.
- Smooth playhead (#69): the player redraws on each refresh of your monitor (60, 120, 144, 240 Hz...) instead of
  30 times a second, and the playhead moves smoothly between audio blocks. Settings > Display > *Animation frame
  rate* caps it (30 to 240 fps) or sets Unlimited.
- Reduce motion (#69): Settings > Display; follows macOS, Windows or GNOME's setting unless you choose. It turns off
  the fade on an accepted genre suggestion; the playhead still moves.

### App icon (#70)
- TrueGrid has its own icon, the beat-grid mark from the header (first beat in cyan), in the Dock, taskbar,
  Alt-Tab and the window title.
- Linux: the download includes a menu entry and icons; run `./install-desktop-entry.sh` once to add TrueGrid to
  your app launcher.

### Export to device: drive tools (#31)
- The preview says how long copying should take, from a short write and read test on the drive.
- Lower-quality copies: when the drive already has, say, a 128 kbps MP3 of a FLAC you're exporting, *Lower-quality
  copies…* lets you pick, file by file, which ones to replace. Both are kept unless you tick one; a replaced copy
  goes to `.truegrid/replaced` on the drive once yours is copied and checked. CLI: `--replace-lower-quality`.
- Mirror mode: music TrueGrid copied in an earlier export that isn't in this one moves to `.truegrid/trash`, so the
  drive holds just this export. Listed and asked about separately; music TrueGrid didn't copy is never moved; undo
  puts it back. CLI: `--mirror`.

The first release: a DJ librarian that analyses your music with KeyTempo, lets you fix and prep it, and takes it
to rekordbox, Serato, Engine DJ, Traktor or straight onto a USB drive for the player.

0.1.0 was never released: its candidates `v0.1.0-rc.1` and `v0.1.0-rc.2` led straight into 0.2.0, which adds
Organisation (below) on top of them. *New since rc.2:* smart crates, My Tags, What mixes next and tags as crates.

### Organisation (#11)
- Smart crates: playlists that fill themselves from rules (BPM range, key and keys that mix with it, genre tag,
  rating, year, date added, playlist and more), with all / any matching and an optional "only the first N".
  File > New smart crate (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N), or *New smart crate* in the sidebar. They export as ordinary playlists.
- Genre tags as crates: File > Export > *Genre tags as crates* adds a *Genres* folder of crates to every export.
- CLI: `smart`, `smart add`, `smart remove`, and `--genre-crates` on the export commands.
- My Tags: labels of your own, in groups if you like, from the track menu, the sidebar (drop tracks on a tag) or
  `truegrid-cli mytags`. Library only; usable in search (`mytag:`), smart crates and exports (as crates).
- What mixes next (Cmd/Ctrl+J): tracks that mix after the selected one, scored on key, tempo (half / double time
  included), genre and My Tags, with the reason in a Match column. CLI: `truegrid-cli next`.
- File > Export > *Tags as crates* now adds My Tags crates beside the genre crates.
- The library moves to schema 10 (smart crate rules, My Tags); older versions of TrueGrid can't open it afterwards.
- Before updating an older library's format, TrueGrid keeps a copy of it as it was beside it
  (`library.schema<N>-backup-<date>.truegrid`). If the copy can't be made, the library isn't changed. *New in rc.2.*

### Library and analysis
- Watched folders, drag and drop, incremental rescans; missing files flagged and found again.
- KeyTempo analysis: BPM to 0.01 with an alternate reading, beat grid and downbeat, key / Camelot / Open Key,
  time signature. Tempo presets per genre family.
- Needs review queue, ×2 / ½ and BPM lock, search filters (`bpm:`, `key:`, `genre:`).
- Duplicate finder with keeper choice; duplicates are left, trashed or moved, never deleted.

### Genre tags and suggestions (#20, #21, #25)
- Several genre tags per track from a built-in library of 18 families, 124 genres and 409 styles, plus your own.
- Genre suggestions from analysis with Likely / Possible / Unsure confidence; nothing reaches files until accepted.

### Your files stay safe (#17)
- Every change to a file is shown and confirmed first; tag writes are backed up, read back and verified.
- History lists every change and can undo it, including duplicate removals and exports.

### Player and track prep (#26)
- Player with waveform, cues, scrubbing, auto-advance and output device choice.
- Grid editing, hot cues A–H, memory cues and loops, ratings and colours, tempo slider with key-lock.

### Appearance (#5, #32, #33)
- Themes, five fonts, text size 90–150%, interface scale up to 200% and row density.

### Menus (#54)
- A menu bar with every command: File, Edit, View, Track, Library, Playback and Help. On macOS it's the system menu
  bar with the usual TrueGrid menu (About, Check for Updates…, Settings…, Quit); on Windows and Linux it runs along
  the top of the window in the current theme, and Alt + a menu's first letter opens it.
- The header keeps the search field, *Export to device…* and (in Duplicates) *Clean up…*; the other buttons moved
  into the menus under the same names. Right-click menus and existing shortcuts work as before.
- New shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+O add folder, +R rescan, +N new playlist, +Shift+I import, +E export to device, +1-5 the
  library views, +A select all, +/ the shortcuts window, +, Settings. Nothing that writes or removes files has one.
- Help > Keyboard shortcuts lists every command and its keys, plus the player's own keys.
- Settings… gathers what was spread over menus and dialogs: writing tags to files and the key notation, asking
  before tag writes, the genre suggestion note, the two update choices, and theme, font and sizes.
- File > Add files… adds single files (before, only by dropping them on the window).

### DJ software (#7, #8)
- Import rekordbox XML, Serato and Engine DJ libraries with a compare-and-merge review.
- Export rekordbox XML, Serato crates, Engine DJ libraries and Traktor NML; Serato cues, loops and grids written
  into audio files. Per-app MP3 timing offsets.

### Export to device (#31)
- One flow to put your library on a USB or SD drive: optional byte-for-byte audio copy, hash-verified, with
  incremental re-exports that never overwrite a file TrueGrid didn't copy.
- Formats on the drive: Engine DJ (Prime / SC), Pioneer CDJ / XDJ (`export.pdb` with grids, cues and waveforms),
  Serato, rekordbox XML and Traktor. The whole export can be undone from History.
- Verify drive (File > *Verify drive…*, `truegrid-cli verify-drive`): reads every copied file back against its
  checksum and checks the Engine DJ database, listing anything changed, damaged or missing. Only reads.

### Updates (#40)
- TrueGrid checks for a newer version shortly after it starts and then daily (Help > Check for updates
  automatically), and Help > Check for Updates… checks now. A banner offers What's new, Download (the release page)
  and Skip this version; nothing is downloaded or installed by the app. Release candidates only with Help > Include
  release candidates.

### Command line
- `truegrid-cli` for scanning, listing, edits, duplicates, imports and every export, with `--dry-run` and `--yes`;
  `truegrid-cli version --check` for updates.

### Known limits
- Builds are not code-signed yet: macOS and Windows warn on first launch (see the README's Download section).
- Not yet checked on real players: Engine DJ and Pioneer exports are tested against format fixtures only.
- OneLibrary (CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO) is not written (#49). History / set import and two-way sync
  come later (#48).
